Class GameController

java.lang.Object
chess.gui.GameController
All Implemented Interfaces:
GameListener
public final class GameController extends Object implements GameListener
Connects the Swing window to the game (the Controller in Model-View-Controller).

Mouse handlers in BoardPanel call squareClicked(Position) or pieceDropped(Position, Position). This class turns those clicks into a Move, asks Game.tryMove(Move) whether it is legal, and tells the GameView what to show. It never checks chess rules itself; every rule lives in the back end.

The controller is also a GameListener: after any accepted move (the human's or the computer's), the game calls onMoveMade(Game, MoveResult), which refreshes the view and, if it is now the computer's turn, starts the computer thinking on a background thread.

All methods must be called on the Swing event dispatch thread.

      private void attemptMove(Position from, Position to)

      from - source square
      to - destination square

    • startComputerTurnIfNeeded

      private void startComputerTurnIfNeeded()
      If it is the computer's turn, chooses its move on a background thread so the window stays responsive, then plays it back on the event dispatch thread. If the strategy fails or returns an illegal move, a random legal move is played instead and the problem is logged.
